summary: The analysis of "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star" (64.8 s, 99.4 BPM, 4/4) is already very consistent: the detected key of D major matches the chord histogram exactly (D 64 beats, G 24, A 16 — pure I–IV–V) with no out-of-key chords, so no set_key or respell is needed. Every chord segment is at least 2 beats long and the G–D–G–D–A–D pattern repeats systematically, so there are no 1-beat blips to merge and no chords are hard enough to warrant simplification. I added a four-part form: an 8-beat chord-only intro (c001), two verse sections matching the two lyrical couplets (l001–l006 and l007–l010, both on the same chord pattern), and an outro covering the repeated closing couplet (l011–l012) ending on a 6-beat D. Capo 0 with D shapes keeps everything in open chords, and a plain "D-DU-UDU" strum suits the 4/4 nursery-rhyme feel. Lyric lines are all short, well-formed sentences with healthy unit durations (min 0.244 s), so no lyric patches were made.
